The book traces the name to the Normans who crossed with William the Conqueror in 1066.
Three origins are offered: the Norse Eystein, "rocky island"; a Viking King Huc of Denmark;
or, most often, the Teutonic Hugh, so that Hutchins is Hugh's son.
In English records it appears as Huchun Aleyn of Wakefield, Yorkshire, in 1277,
and as Huchon and Huchin in Sussex, Suffolk and Worcestershire by the 1320s.
